questions.question_text: Which one of these random variables is continuous?

options.text: The volume of petrol, in litres, pumped into a car
The number of goals scored in a football match
options.why: Goals are counted, so the values go up in separate whole-number steps.

options.text: The number of eggs in a carton
options.why: Eggs are counted, so only whole-number values are possible.

options.text: The shoe size chosen from the sizes a shop stocks
options.why: The sizes stocked form a listed set of separate values, so the variable is discrete.

questions.solution_text:
Petrol volume is measured, so it can take any value in an interval.
The other three are counts or a listed set of sizes.
The volume of petrol is the continuous variable.

questions.question_text:
The temperature at noon is recorded to the nearest whole degree Celsius.
Which statement about the true temperature before rounding is correct?

options.text: It is continuous, because temperature can take any value in an interval even though the record is rounded
It is discrete, because the recorded values are whole numbers
options.why: Treats the rounding of the record as if it were the values the quantity itself can take.

options.text: It is discrete, because only finitely many temperatures occur during the year
options.why: Counts the recorded outcomes rather than asking whether the quantity is measured.

options.text: It is continuous, because more than $30$ different values are possible
options.why: Confuses having many possible values with filling a whole interval.

questions.solution_text:
Temperature is measured, so the true value can be anywhere in an interval.
The rounded record is discrete, but the question asks about the true temperature.
The true temperature is continuous.

questions.question_text:
For a randomly chosen student, let $H$ be the true height in centimetres, $R$ the height recorded to the nearest $0.1$ cm, and $N$ the number of days absent this term.
Which classification is correct?

options.why: Treats the rounded record as continuous, although its possible values occur in separate steps of $0.1$ cm.
Treats true height as a set of isolated values and a whole-number count of absent days as continuous.
Treats both a rounded record and a count as continuous merely because they can have many possible values.

questions.solution_text:
$H$ is continuous because true height can take any value in an interval.
$R$ is discrete because recorded heights occur in separate steps of $0.1$ cm.
$N$ is discrete because absent days are counted in whole numbers.
